transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Dan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO, CedarLane), Liam O'Connor (Head of Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE. Dan from our solutions team is here as well. How's everyone?
[00:06] Priya Kapoor: Hi Maya, thanks. Doing good. We've been trying to carve out time for this — appreciate it.
[00:10] Dan Ortiz: Hey Priya, Liam, Sofia — quick agenda from my side: understand your workload, isolation/compliance needs, traffic patterns, and then talk through Dedicated options — reserved GPUs, burst, scaling, and benchmarks.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Sounds great. We're evaluating host vs dedicated vs private but leaning dedicated because of data isolation and predictable latency.
[00:26] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, and we have SOC2, customer data residency concerns and need KMS integration.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Perfect. Maybe we start with current stack — what are you running today, model sizes, inference volume?
[00:36] Priya Kapoor: Right now it's a mix — we've got a model team running a proprietary 13B model in prod, a smaller 2.7B for lower latency tasks. Production traffic is modest now, roughly 10 million tokens a month, but our roadmap anticipates spiky traffic up to 50-60M tokens/mo during campaigns, and possible growth to 200M within 12 months if a new feature launches.
[00:58] Dan Ortiz: When you say spiky, what's the burst pattern — short sharp bursts or sustained uplift over hours?
[01:04] Priya Kapoor: Mostly sharp bursts, like 10-20x baseline for a few minutes to an hour. Example: when our marketing sends out in-app prompts during fintech events.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Also some sustained increases over a day during reporting windows. We need guaranteed throughput for peak periods.
[01:18] Dan Ortiz: Got it. Dedicated can support reserved capacity with configured burst headroom. We typically size a dedicated pool as N GPUs reserved, with autoscaler policies that allow temporary burst to a larger pool from a shared burst capacity or cloud burst.
[01:30] Sofia Alvarez: For compliance, does Redwood provide a private control plane or do we need Private for VPC-only control?
[01:36] Maya Chen: Good question. Our Dedicated offering gives you a logically isolated GPU pool with tenant separation and dedicated network segments; for stricter network requirements we offer Redwood Private — a customer-managed control plane or on-prem option. Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints for traffic.
[01:50] Priya Kapoor: And key management — can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
[01:54] Dan Ortiz: Yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. We can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs for encryption at rest and in transit.
[02:02] Liam O'Connor: How do you handle KV cache and model warm starts? Bursts mean cold-start latency could be a problem.
[02:08] Dan Ortiz: We do prefix/KV caching and keep a hot pool warm to reduce cold-starts. For very spiky traffic we recommend a small always-on baseline with reserved GPUs and configure pre-warming or scheduled warm pools for predictable events. There's also an option for instant burst via cloud-bursting where compatible model variants run in hosted clusters — but that has data routing considerations.
[02:26] Priya Kapoor: That hosted fallback is a concern — data residency and customer data hitting shared hosted infra may be a blocker.
[02:32] Maya Chen: Understood. We can architect bursts to stay within your Dedicated footprint where possible. If you need absolute on-prem isolation, Redwood Private is the safe bet. For Dedicated we can set routing policies to prefer dedicated nodes and only fall back to verified variants if explicitly allowed.
[02:46] Sofia Alvarez: On the SLA side — what's typical latency SLO you can support for a 13B model?
[02:52] Dan Ortiz: For quantized 13B and optimized kernels we routinely hit 150-300ms per token depending on sequence length and batch settings. If you need sub-100ms tail latency at scale that's more challenging and usually requires heavier quantization, model distillation, or multiple GPU sharding. We can run benchmarks with your payload to give concrete numbers.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: Cost is obviously a factor. Do you have rough committed pricing for, say, a pool of 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved vs pay-as-you-go?
[03:24] Maya Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet after the call. Committed reserved capacity is usually ~40-60% discount vs on-demand, depending on term length and commit size. We'll model scenarios for 50M and 200M tokens/mo.
[03:36] Priya Kapoor: Great. For scaling — if we start with, say, 4 GPUs reserved and hit a sustained 2x for a week, how does autoscaling and billing work?
[03:44] Dan Ortiz: You can set autoscale to add burst nodes — billing for Dedicated burst is prorated hourly; committed reserve covers baseline and discounts apply only to the reserved units. We can also configure burst caps to control spend.
[03:55] Sofia Alvarez: We need auditability — do you expose request-level audit logs, token-level cost breakdowns, and RBAC for routes?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Yes. Redwood Console provides per-route metrics, token-level cost, tracing hooks, and audit logs. RBAC and SSO/SAML integrations are available for user access controls.
[04:12] Priya Kapoor: What about multi-tenancy inside our org — we have separate business units that need logical separation.
[04:18] Dan Ortiz: Within Dedicated you can create per-team routes with RBAC and per-route quotas, and per-team model pins. Logs and usage can be scoped by team. For strong separation between BU's you can provision separate dedicated pools.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: Any constraints around GPU types and model compatibility? We may want to run different architectures.
[04:34] Dan Ortiz: We support common transformer architectures. Kernel selection and quantization profiles are chosen per-model. We can mix GPU types but it's simplest to standardize on one class for predictable performance.
[04:44] Priya Kapoor: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[04:47] Dan Ortiz: Ideally a sample workload: representative prompts, sequence length distribution, desired qps, and a small dataset for quality checks. We'll instrument client-side metrics and run the test in a staging dedicated pool or a reserved test cluster.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: We can put that together.
[05:01] Maya Chen: Next steps — we'll send pricing, the SOC2 pack, and propose benchmark windows. Dan will draft the benchmark plan. Anything else?
[05:09] Sofia Alvarez: Please include details on BYOK + HSM integration, and the audit log retention options. Also we need a data flow diagram for how requests move between our VPC and Redwood.
[05:19] Maya Chen: Noted.
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: Timeline question — we're hoping to have a pilot running by late June. Is that doable?
[05:25] Dan Ortiz: Yes, assuming we align on sizing and security checks. Benchmarks early next week would help.
[05:31] Priya Kapoor: Good. Any potential blockers you foresee?
[05:34] Dan Ortiz: Main blockers are compliance sign-offs and network setup. If you require on-prem Private, that takes longer. Dedicated is usually a 2-6 week provisioning + validation depending on procurement.
[05:45] Maya Chen: I'll work with you on procurement and get legal and security materials over.
[05:48] Priya Kapoor: Thanks.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Alright, we'll follow up with docs and pricing. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-recognitions (e.g., 'Informant' for 'Infopoint' maybe), some run-on lines and filler words left intact.
